Hey all. I'm basically a chess newb of the highest order, but I've been getting steadily more interested in it the last few months ever since a friend and I started playing semi regular games. Oh jeez, the Sicilian is wild and complex. I myself play the French Defense mainly, I suggest you look into it it's a pretty great opening. Basically the Sicilian is effective because it has a lot of theory and sharp lines involved where one mistake can ruin your whole opening. It is also one of the more aggressive openings for black. Given that you appear to be a bit newer I highly suggest you learn a simple opening for e4 and d4 and c4 maybe and focus on tactics, the reason being if you try to go in with more complex openings with a lot of lines you can find yourself in a line you don't know and get just demolished.

for e4 I would look into responding with e5 and going into a normal sort of game. For d4 the Queens gambit is good and has some cool lines to look into. Also as a side note if you find yourself playing someone more skilled as white I would suggest you open with d4 as it's much more passive and doesn't have a bunch of terrifying lines like e4.

The sicilian is a pretty sharp opening. My overall thoughts on this are: if you play it more, you'll get better at it. There's one thing to be said for theory, but its quite another thing to see all the moves over and over again in your own games.

The general rules I follow are: 1. Don't play d6 until you see Nf3 2. Consider changing over to the dragon at all times 3. Consider a b pawn push in order to activate your light-squared bishop. 4. Watch out for tactics on your f2 pawn. 5. Consider e6 as some people have said for a bit more king safety.

As for why It counters the kings gambit, IMHO it mostly just ignores it and gains a lot of attacks on those pawns.
